text.p: These are the leading stories in Zambia's newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and can not vouch for their accuracy.
- An unprecedented 100 independent candidates will run for Parliament in what promises to be the most heavily contested poll in history on November 18, the Elections Office said.

- The Zambia National Farmers Union said it had bought over 100 tonnes of maize from farmers unable to find a market for their crop. Union spokesman Vajay Vashee said thousands of maize bags remained uncollected across the country and could be damaged by rains.

- An opposition politician on Tuesday appeared in court after being arrested for collecting voters cards in an opposition 'don't vote' campaign. He was charged with being in unlawful possession of the documents.
- Civic groups have urged the Electoral Commission to call off the November 18 polls because the opposition is succeeding in its campaign to get people to boycott the elections.
